analyzed_vuln.description: The user-defined `key.hash` dispatch in `obj_hash_code` is guarded by `h_check_modified`, but that guard only compares representation flags and table/EA pointers and capacity; it does not compare the Hash size or `ea_n_used`. A reentrant `hash` callback can therefore structurally insert/delete entries without reallocating, evade the modification check, and corrupt an in-progress index rebuild. In this PoV the inconsistent state ultimately leaves a stale String backing pointer, which is read by `mrb_byte_hash_step` through `mrb_str_hash_m`, producing the heap-use-after-free. The patch should strengthen the modification validation used around callback dispatch (especially size/used-entry state), or prevent callbacks from observing/mutating a partially built table.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Ruby input creates a Hash at the 16-entry AR limit with at least one non-primitive key whose `hash` method executes Ruby code, then inserts a 17th distinct entry. `ar_set` converts AR to HT and `ht_init`/`ib_init` re-hashes existing keys. During that callback, Ruby code structurally mutates the same Hash in a way that changes size or used entries without changing the table pointer, EA pointer, capacity, or checked flags, so `h_check_modified` fails to reject it. Continued bucket construction/use of the corrupted state eventually invokes `String#hash` on an object whose heap buffer has already been freed.

patch_result.patch:
--- a/mruby/src/hash.c
+++ b/mruby/src/hash.c
@@ -262,6 +262,8 @@
   struct RHash *h__ = h;                                                        \
   uint32_t mask__ = MRB_HASH_HT|MRB_HASH_IB_BIT_MASK|MRB_HASH_AR_EA_CAPA_MASK;  \
   uint32_t flags__ = h__->flags & mask__;                                       \
+  uint32_t size__ = h_size(h__);                                                 \
+  uint32_t ea_n_used__ = h_ht_p(h__) ? ht_ea_n_used(h__) : ar_ea_n_used(h__);   \
   void* tbl__ = (mrb_assert(h__->hsh.ht), h__->hsh.ht);                         \
   uint32_t ht_ea_capa__ = 0;                                                    \
   hash_entry *ht_ea__ = NULL;                                                   \
@@ -273,11 +275,13 @@
   }                                                                             \
   code;                                                                         \
   if (flags__ != (h__->flags & mask__) ||                                       \
-      tbl__ != h__->hsh.ht ||                                                       \
+      tbl__ != h__->hsh.ht ||                                                   \
+      size__ != h_size(h__) ||                                                  \
       ((H_CHECK_MODIFIED_USE_HT_EA_CAPA_FOR_AR || h_ht_p(h__)) &&               \
        ht_ea_capa__ != ht_ea_capa(h__)) ||                                      \
       ((H_CHECK_MODIFIED_USE_HT_EA_FOR_AR || h_ht_p(h__)) &&                    \
-       ht_ea__ != ht_ea(h__))) {                                                \
+       ht_ea__ != ht_ea(h__)) ||                                                \
+      ea_n_used__ != (h_ht_p(h__) ? ht_ea_n_used(h__) : ar_ea_n_used(h__))) {   \
     mrb_raise(mrb, E_RUNTIME_ERROR, "hash modified");                           \
   }                                                                             \
 } while (0)

args: Analyze the reentrancy vulnerability around obj_hash_code(), h_check_modified(), AR-to-HT conversion, ht_init()/ib_init(), and user-defined key.hash callbacks in src/hash.c. Which state fields must be snapshotted and checked to reliably detect structural mutation, and are there other callback dispatch sites using the same guard? Recommend a minimal root-cause patch preserving behavior.

The reported ASan crash is a heap-use-after-free in mrb_byte_hash_step via mrb_str_hash_m, called from obj_hash_code at src/hash.c around line 345 while ar_set converts a 16-entry AR hash to HT for a 17th insertion. A user key's Ruby hash callback mutates the same Hash during index rebuilding. The current h_check_modified reportedly compares representation flags, table/EA pointers, and capacity but omits logical size and ea_n_used, allowing same-allocation insert/delete mutation to evade detection. I have not yet patched anything; I am examining the exact structs and guard call sites to choose between extending the snapshot/check and preventing callbacks during partial construction.
